guides.title: ESCVDO in Lima: The Peruvian Fashion House Weaving Heritage Forward
guides.dek: A closer look at Peruvian textile craft, ESCVDO’s artisan network and how to check Barranco studio events before visiting.
guides.body:
In Lima’s Barranco district, old villas, artist studios and gardens meet the soft gray light of the Pacific. The neighborhood rewards a slower kind of looking—the same attention that brings the work of ESCVDO into focus. The Peruvian fashion house builds contemporary silhouettes through ancestral weaving, organic fibers and the patient intelligence of handwork.

ESCVDO’s clothes feel rooted without becoming nostalgic. Crochet dresses skim the body with graphic precision; loom-woven skirts turn color into rhythm; braided tassels and hand-applied fringe make movement part of the design. Each piece carries Peru’s coast, highlands and Amazon not as a motif pasted onto fashion, but as a living network of material, technique and people.

Barranco and the Art of Looking Closely

Barranco is an apt home for a label committed to both continuity and experimentation. ESCVDO’s own archive notes that its Lima studio opens twice a year for a special archive sale, inviting visitors to encounter samples and earlier collections in person. That studio culture mirrors the district itself: intimate, creative and connected to the value of objects made to last.

The destination context extends far beyond the capital. The brand describes an artisan network spanning Peru’s three natural regions. Organic Pima cotton comes from the coastal region of Pisco; alpaca is sourced from the Andes; plant-based materials and techniques connect to communities in the Amazon.

A Fashion House Built Around Craft

ESCVDO was created to honor Peru’s textile legacy while reimagining it through contemporary design. Its sustainability platform identifies three guiding pillars: valuing and fairly compensating artisanal work, trusting community collaboration, and caring for the planet through traceability and lower-waste production.

The house reports working with more than 350 artisans, 95 percent of them women and 91 percent from rural areas. It also states that 80 percent of its clothing is produced by preorder, a model intended to limit overproduction and foreground the time behind each piece. These numbers matter because the craft is not decorative—it is the structure of the business.

The Pieces and Techniques to Notice

  • Hand-crocheted dresses and sets: graphic, body-aware silhouettes made from pure cotton, with the subtle variations that mark genuine handwork.
  • Pedal-loom weaving: seen in pieces such as the ICA skirt, created with artisans from Huancavelica and developed through a zero-waste loom process.
  • Peruvian Pima cotton: sourced by the brand from Pisco and prized for long fibers, softness and suitability for intricate textile work.
  • Andean alpaca: a light, warm fiber that connects the wardrobe to the highlands while remaining luxurious enough for international travel.
  • HUARI Pre-Spring 2026: a current collection inspired by the pre-Inca Huari civilization, translating geometry, mineral color and cosmological motifs into layered cotton textures, tunics and dresses.

The Jet Set LatAM Styling Perspective

Let texture lead. In Lima, pair an ivory crochet skirt with a silk tank, flat leather sandals and a sculptural cuff. For the Sacred Valley, layer a woven tunic over narrow trousers and add an alpaca wrap for the temperature shift. A hand-crocheted maxi dress needs little more than sunlit skin, a low bun and one strong bag.

Because many pieces already hold complex pattern and surface, the most modern styling feels quiet around them. Choose tonal accessories, clean shapes and natural materials. The result should feel collected and intentional—not themed.

Continue the Peru Mood

Open the Full Luxe Jetter Experience →

How to Visit and Shop

Start with the official ESCVDO website for current collections, preorder information, composition and care. Handmade crochet and woven pieces can vary slightly, so read each size guide and allow time for preorder production. If you are in Lima, check the brand’s official channels for studio events and archive-sale dates before visiting Barranco.

Continue the fashion journey with our guide to São Paulo’s designer boutiques in Jardins, then discover how Luxe Jetter turns destination style into a shoppable experience.

A Future Woven by Hand

ESCVDO makes a persuasive case for fashion that moves forward by looking carefully at what already exists: skilled hands, regional fibers, living techniques and the knowledge held within communities. The clothes are beautiful because they are contemporary. They are meaningful because the path from fiber to finished piece remains visible.

guides.title: Discover Boutique Shopping in Santiago: Barrio Italia & Vitacura
guides.dek: Two design stops and an artisan-cookie pause in Barrio Italia, with Vitacura kept as a separate outing.
guides.body:
Jet Set Shopping Notes · Santiago · Barrio Italia

Shoes, handmade jewelry and something sweet: a compact Barrio Italia edit that leaves time to look closely at Chilean design.

Your shopping afternoon at a glance

The edit: 2 shopping stops + a sweets pause

The walk: 100 metres · about 1 minute between the two buildings

Look for: Footwear, jewelry and independent design

Make time: Allow two to three hours for browsing and a pause

Researched 27 September 2026. A suggested route, not a claim of a personal visit. Price snapshots are online examples; store prices and stock may differ.

Barrio Italia first; Vitacura as a separate outing

Santiago’s fashion scene brings together Chilean craftsmanship and contemporary design. Barrio Italia offers independent shops and galleries; Vitacura suits a separate afternoon around its boutiques, while Lastarria connects shopping with culture. This refreshed route concentrates on Avenida Italia instead of presenting Barrio Italia and Vitacura as neighboring stops.

Two buildings are enough to give the afternoon a shape: start with footwear, move into the gallery for jewelry and other independent shops, then pause for something sweet. The short distance is an advantage—you can spend your time browsing rather than crossing the city.

01 · The designer edit

Burano

Avenida Italia 1449, Providencia, Santiago, Chile

Make footwear your starting point. Burano’s range includes sandals, loafers, boots and other leather styles; try the shape that works with your everyday wardrobe, and ask about fit and care before deciding.

Official details → · Find this stop →

02 · The designer edit

Ada Vásquez Orfebre — Bodega Italia

Avenida Italia 1337, local 5, Providencia, Santiago, Chile

This handmade-jewelry stop brings a smaller-scale purchase into the afternoon. Look at the finish and weight of earrings or a ring, and ask which metal and surface treatment were used. The gallery directory also lists other fashion and design shops if you want to browse further.

Official details → · Find this stop →

03 · The sweet pause

Nanai Cookies — Bodega Italia

Avenida Italia 1337, local 14, Providencia, Santiago, Chile

End with an artisan-cookie stop in the same gallery. This is a sweets pause rather than a promised full-service café; choose from the day’s selection and keep a longer meal for the next part of your day.

Official details → · Find this stop →

Walk the edit

  1. Burano — Avenida Italia 1449, Providencia, Santiago, Chile
  2. Ada Vásquez Orfebre — Bodega Italia — Avenida Italia 1337, local 5, Providencia, Santiago, Chile
  3. Nanai Cookies — Bodega Italia — Avenida Italia 1337, local 14, Providencia, Santiago, Chile

Google Maps estimate when checked: 100 metres · about 1 minute between the two buildings. Allow extra time for crossings, browsing and your café stop. Confirm same-day opening hours before setting out.

Open or share the walking route →

Make the purchase count

Ask about sizing, materials and exchanges before buying shoes or jewelry. Prices vary by piece; the linked official catalogues are the place to check current Chilean-peso prices. A lower sticker price is not automatically the better choice if the fit or care requirements do not suit you.

The route ends at Bodega Italia’s entrance; Ada Vásquez and Nanai are separate units inside. Allow time to find them, and check each business’s hours rather than assuming the gallery schedule applies to every tenant.

For the next part of the trip, open the Santiago city guide, three-day itinerary, and Santiago food guide. Explore more Latin American fashion with Luxe Jetter, or plan your travel wardrobe in the Luxe Jetter app.

A note on the previous route

The earlier guide joined Barrio Italia and Vitacura in one walking circuit. This update replaces that route with currently verified addresses on Avenida Italia. Vitacura remains a separate neighborhood option; omitted businesses are not being described as closed.

guides.title: Montevideo by Cruiser Bike: La Rambla Rides and Vintage Charm
guides.dek: A slower look at Montevideo’s Rambla, Ciudad Vieja and Parque Rodó. Use the story for inspiration and check current cycling conditions locally.
guides.body:
Montevideo by Cruiser bike. Follow the curve of Uruguay’s coast and feel Montevideo unfold with every turn. Cruiser biking along La Rambla — the city’s iconic waterfront boulevard — blends seaside calm, vintage character, and a rhythm that’s effortlessly slow.

Quick Links: ✈ Flights  |  🏨 Hotels  |  🎟 Montevideo Bike Tours

The Long Ride Along the Sea

Montevideo’s La Rambla stretches for more than 13 miles, a sweeping promenade hugging the Río de la Plata. Locals call it their front porch — a place for biking, mate sipping, and sunset watching. The pace is unhurried, the view infinite.

Start your ride near Punta Carretas, where modern towers overlook small beaches and coastal parks. The path is smooth, wide, and welcoming, with benches and shaded palms inviting you to pause. As you ride, waves lap against the rocks below and the city hums quietly behind you — a blend of ocean serenity and urban charm.

Vintage Streets and Café Stops

Head inland toward Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo’s old town, where cobblestones and colonial façades whisper stories of the city’s maritime past. Here, bikes glide through narrow lanes lined with antique stores, bookstores, and cafés that seem suspended in time. Stop for a cortado at a shaded terrace, or linger in Plaza Matriz, watching artists sketch and musicians play.

Guided bike tours often trace these routes, sharing the layers of Uruguay’s quiet capital — its independence, its poetry, its deep connection to the sea.

👉 Browse Montevideo Bike Tours on TripAdvisor

Moments Between Land and Water

One of the city’s most beautiful stops is Parque Rodó, a lakeside oasis framed by art nouveau pavilions and lush gardens. It’s where couples stroll, friends gather for picnics, and cyclists circle slowly around the water. From here, rejoin the Rambla heading west for sunset — a daily ritual where locals gather with thermoses of yerba mate, sharing conversation as the sky fades from coral to lavender.

When to Ride

Montevideo enjoys a temperate climate year-round, but March to May and September to November bring ideal biking conditions — clear skies and gentle breezes. Morning rides promise golden light over the river, while evenings glow warm and wind-soft along the coast.

What to Bring

Lightweight layers for coastal winds Flat shoes and relaxed clothing for easy movement Sunglasses, sunscreen, and a water bottle A small pouch or basket for snacks or your mate cup — locals will approve

In a world that moves too fast, there’s an art to slowing down—and the journey becomes the destination. In “Cruiser Bike Adventures Across Latin America: Slow Travel at Its Best,” we trade the typical tour bus for two sun-lit wheels and discover a rhythm of travel that feels less like racing and more like roaming. Whether you’re gliding through Buenos Aires’ grand boulevards, coasting along Cartagena’s pastel Caribbean walls, or exploring Mexico City’s vibrant Sunday ciclovía, the cruiser bike connects you to culture, light, and local stories in a deeply human way. Click through to begin your slow-travel story:

Cruiser Bike Adventures Across Latin America →

The Montevideo Mood

There’s a saying here: “El tiempo pasa despacio en la Rambla.” Time passes slowly along the Rambla. That’s the essence of this ride — an experience that feels less like sightseeing and more like breathing in rhythm with the city. You’ll see fishermen casting lines, children learning to skate, and old friends sharing quiet moments — all under a sky that seems to stretch forever.

Montevideo reminds you that luxury can be simplicity: sunlight, conversation, and motion in perfect balance.

guides.title: Cycling Mendoza’s Wine Roads: A Beautiful Day Through Maipú
guides.dek: A Maipú cycling day with space for reservations, changing weather and a planned return transfer.
guides.body:
Cycling Adventures · Mendoza, Argentina

A sunlit day through Maipú, where vineyards, olive groves and Andean air reward the traveler who slows down.

Morning in Maipú begins with long shadows across the vines. On a bicycle, Mendoza’s wine country feels intimate: irrigation channels beside the road, poplars lifting into a blue sky and the Andes holding the horizon.

Maipú is the classic introduction to cycling the region because wineries, olive producers and bike operators can be joined into a compact circuit. The pleasure depends on planning lightly but carefully—few reservations, realistic distance and a safe return that never treats wine tasting casually.

A graceful one-day route

10:00 · Fit and mapChoose the correct frame size, test brakes and gears, secure a helmet and review road surfaces.

Late morning · First estateBook one focused tour before the heat rises, leaving generous time between stops.

Afternoon · Lunch and returnMake the final tasting optional and arrange a transfer if alcohol, wind or fatigue changes the plan.

Season, weather and pacing

Mendoza has an arid continental climate with strong seasonal contrasts. Summer can be hot and stormy; winter is cold and dry, with possible nighttime frost. Spring and autumn often offer comfortable riding, though wind and temperature changes still matter.

Start early, protect exposed skin and carry more water than you expect to need. If heat, wind, rain or low visibility arrives, change plans. A booked experience is never a reason to ride in conditions that feel unsafe.

Safety first: Mendoza requires cyclists to use an approved helmet and front white and rear red lights. Alcohol impairs balance and judgment; if tastings are central, limit consumption or organize a bike pickup and vehicle transfer. Confirm the current rules before departure.

Accessibility and practical logistics

Ask the rental operator about step-through frames, e-bikes, mechanical support, road gradients and accessible transfer alternatives. Some official city areas have extensive cycle lanes, but vineyard routes can include shared roads and uneven shoulders. Riders who prefer not to cycle can use a guided vehicle tour or wine bus.

Pack breathable layers, closed shoes, sunglasses, sunscreen, a small first-aid kit, phone battery and offline confirmations. Operators may set fixed collection and return hours, so confirm those before reserving wineries.

Extend the journey

Build a longer Argentina itinerary

For pacing, connections and beautiful multi-stop logic, use our guide to planning a multi-destination Latin America trip.

A Maipú cycling day is memorable because it refuses to hurry. The vines become landscape rather than backdrop, lunch has room to linger and the route itself becomes as meaningful as the glass waiting at the next stop.

Sources: City of Mendoza tourism; Government of Mendoza road-safety guidance; official Mendoza tourism provider directory; Visit Argentina. Verified September 2026.

guides.title: PeruRail Titicaca: The Beautiful Day Train From Cusco to Puno
guides.dek: A full-day rail journey from Cusco to Puno, with operational checks, changing scenery and time set aside for the journey.
guides.body:
The departure from Cusco begins in cool Andean light. By evening, the train reaches Puno with the high plateau glowing outside the windows—a full day in which the journey, not simply the arrival, becomes the story.

Across the Altiplano by Rail

PeruRail Titicaca links Cusco and Puno on a daylong route through the Peruvian Andes. The official timetable lists morning departures and evening arrivals, with service days varying by direction. Landscapes shift from the Cusco valley toward broad altiplano country before the line approaches Lake Titicaca.

This is slow travel in its most cinematic form: time to watch villages, peaks and grasslands change rather than compressing southern Peru into another airport transfer.

The Experience

Reserve the day for the train. Dress for changing temperatures, keep a camera close and allow the scenery to set the pace. A window seat is desirable, but shared spaces and observation areas can offer different views throughout the journey. Dining and onboard programming may vary, so confirm exactly what is included with your fare.

Seasonal Planning

Conditions in the Andes can change quickly. The drier months generally bring clearer views and colder mornings; the wetter season can bring dramatic clouds and occasional transport disruption. PeruRail posted a temporary bimodal operation after August 2026 rockfalls and subsequently announced the resumption of Titicaca service. That recent history is a useful reminder to recheck official operational notices shortly before travel.

Altitude, Safety and Accessibility

  • Acclimatize: both Cusco and Puno sit at high altitude. Plan quiet time before the journey, hydrate and follow medical advice appropriate to you.
  • Move carefully: use handrails and take your time when walking through a moving train.
  • Pack medication: keep essential medicine in your personal bag, never out of reach.
  • Confirm access: ask PeruRail directly about boarding assistance, steps, wheelchair dimensions and accessible facilities before purchase.
  • Protect your buffer: avoid a tight same-day flight connection after a long overland journey.

What to Pack

Bring light layers, a warm jacket, sun protection, water, lip balm and a compact power bank. Keep valuables close and choose shoes with grip. A soft scarf earns its space: it warms a cool carriage and looks polished at arrival.

If this journey is part of a longer itinerary, our multi-destination Latin America planning guide will help you build sensible buffers between cities.

Make the rails part of the adventure

Plan the Next Chapter With Rallii Rail

Save scenic train ideas and let the journey between destinations become part of the experience.

Explore Rallii Rail

The Jet Set LatAM Verdict

Choose PeruRail Titicaca when the view matters as much as the destination. It offers the rare luxury of a full day devoted to looking outward—and an elegant way to understand the scale of southern Peru before Lake Titicaca appears.

Sources: PeruRail official resumption notice and schedule; PeruRail operational update. Always verify current schedules, inclusions and service notices directly before booking.
